Permian Resources permitted this deep Wolfcamp stack lateral only yesterday, making this the earliest possible engagement point before any fluid vendor has locked in the contract. Newpark has strong presence in their Delaware program but their Midland Basin fluid awards are less consolidated, making this a genuine open competition if contacted before end of July.

This Hunton re-entry in Canadian County was permitted just yesterday and no mud contract language has appeared in state filings, meaning the fluids decision is genuinely open. Halliburton Baroid is the incumbent on adjacent Chaparral wellbores but a targeted proposal emphasizing HPWBM inhibition performance in Hunton carbonates submitted before September 1 could displace the incumbent before rig arrival.

Rockcliff's Panola County permit was filed only yesterday, making this the earliest possible intervention point before any fluid vendor has been engaged—permit-fresh timing is your highest-value entry window. At 17,900 ft and an estimated 352°F, this well demands a high-performance synthetic system; positioning now with a thermal-stability data package specific to deep East Texas Haynesville gives you a clear differentiator over Newpark's standard pitch.

ConocoPhillips/Burlington Resources runs a Q4 basin-wide fluid contract renewal in October, meaning this September well sits just outside that umbrella and will be sourced independently, giving competitors a narrow entry point before M-I SWACO auto-renews. A well-timed technical presentation to the Dickinson AFE team in early August, emphasizing NPT reduction data from comparable Bakken wells, could secure this standalone award.

Birch Creek is a smaller independent with no long-term master service agreement in place for drilling fluids, making this a greenfield sales opportunity for any major fluids vendor willing to offer day-rate pricing. The permit was filed just yesterday and the procurement contact is still being established — first mover advantage is high if you call before July 30.
